title: Combination Sum II
statement: Return every unique combination of `candidates` that sums to `target`. Each number may be used once. Two combinations that use the same values the same number of times are the same. Sort each combination and sort the list.
hints: Sort so equal values are adjacent and combinations are built in non-decreasing order.
A candidate may be skipped or taken, but it may not be reused, so the next call starts at the next index.
If the current value equals the previous value and the previous value was skipped at this level, skip this one too. That removes duplicate combinations.

approaches.name: All subsets
approaches.explanation: Filter the subsets that hit the target and unique them.

editorial: The recursion state is the start index and the remaining sum. At each level, iterate candidates from the start. Skip a value that repeats the previous one unless that previous one was used in this same level, which the index check `i > start` encodes. Stop the loop when the candidate exceeds the remainder. Record a copy of the path when the remainder hits zero.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def combination_sum_ii(candidates: list[int], target: int) -> list[list[int]]:
    candidates = sorted(candidates)
    out: list[list[int]] = []
    path: list[int] = []

    def dfs(start: int, remain: int) -> None:
        if remain == 0:
            out.append(path[:])
            return
        for i in range(start, len(candidates)):
            if i > start and candidates[i] == candidates[i - 1]:
                continue
            if candidates[i] > remain:
                break
            path.append(candidates[i])
            dfs(i + 1, remain - candidates[i])
            path.pop()

    dfs(0, target)
    return out
